assumptions: The file is PDB, PDBx/mmCIF or core CIF as deposited.
limits: Reports what the depositor wrote, including declarations that may be wrong.
Reading only: no geometry validation or refinement.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: A reader: the structure file's chains, residues and coordinates as written, with nothing inferred.
bio.jane/contract.question: What is in this structure file: chains, sequences, ligands, solvent, disulfides, modified residues, B-factors, cell, resolution and experiment?

description: Read a structure file — PDB, PDBx/mmCIF, or a core CIF small-molecule crystal structure — and report what is in it: the chains and what kind each is, their sequences, the ligands and ordered solvent, the disulfides, the residues the depositor declared modified, the temperature-factor range, the unit cell and space group, the resolution and the experiment. Use it to answer what a structure IS before deciding what to do with it, or to pull a chain's sequence out of a structure so it can be aligned, back-translated or ordered. Reading only: it never writes a structure file and never applies symmetry, so every count it reports is a count of what the file actually holds — for a core CIF that is the asymmetric unit, not the whole cell.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

model.description: which model of an ensemble to describe, 1-based. An NMR entry holds many complete conformers and they are alternatives rather than parts, so the counts always describe ONE of them. The upper bound is the FILE's, so it is not declared here — an out-of-range model is refused by name, with the range that exists.

text.description: the coordinate file's contents — a PDB flat file, a PDBx/mmCIF, or a core CIF; the format is read from the bytes, not from a name, because .cif is shared by two unrelated dictionaries.

name: read_structure

bFactor.description: min, max and mean isotropic B over every atom, or null when the file states none

cell.description: unit cell and space group, absent for a determination with no crystal

chains.description: one row per chain: id, polymer kind, residue and atom counts, the author numbering range, and the observed one-letter sequence

dialect.description: the same answer in words, for a reply to quote

extent.description: the longest side of the bounding box in angstroms — whether this will fit a pore, a groove or a box

format.description: which reader actually ran: `pdb`, `mmcif`, or `smallcif` for a core CIF (small-molecule crystallography, which shares the .cif extension with mmCIF and is a different dictionary)

formula.description: the empirical formula the file STATES about itself (`_chemical_formula_sum`), empty when it states none. For a crystal structure it describes the contents of the CELL, so it can name more atoms than the sites listed

hasPolymer.description: whether any chain is a polymer. False for a core CIF and for a coordinate set holding only a ligand — where `chains`, `residues` and `sequences` describe a wrapper rather than a molecule, and `atoms` is a count of symmetry-independent SITES

hasResolution.description: whether the entry states a resolution at all

helices.description: helices the DEPOSITOR annotated (not a calculation over the coordinates)

id.description: the 4-character entry id the file declares about itself, empty when it declares none

ligands.description: non-water heteroatom components with how many copies of each — the ions, cofactors and bound compounds

method.description: the experimental technique(s) — genuinely more than one for a neutron/X-ray structure

models.description: conformers in the file; more than one means an ensemble

modified.description: modified residues with the standard residue each stands in for, from the file's own MODRES / _pdbx_struct_mod_residue — the only authoritative source for what a component like MSE IS

residues.description: residues in the model described, solvent included

resolution.description: diffraction limit in angstroms. 0 means the entry states NONE (an NMR determination has no resolution) — read `hasResolution` rather than treating 0 as sub-angstrom

sequences.description: the CONSTRUCT sequence per chain as the file declares it (SEQRES / _entity_poly), which includes residues that were never resolved

warnings.description: lines the reader could not parse, named rather than dropped

waters.description: ordered solvent molecules, counted separately from ligands
